target.title: fix(microsoft-foundry): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in az login
target.body:
## Summary

- add stdout/stderr `error` handlers for interactive `az login --use-device-code`
- align the stream-error path with the established `src/node-host/invoke.ts` lifecycle pattern: record the first stream error, send one SIGTERM, escalate to SIGKILL after a grace period, and settle from the child `close` event (with a bounded fallback for shells that never emit `close`)
- keep duplicate stream errors and late child `error` events idempotent: the first stream error wins and teardown runs once
- cover the lifecycle with mocked-timer regressions plus a real spawned local `az` substitute process over real stdio pipes
- collision check: no open PR found for the Microsoft Foundry az login stream-error issue or `extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.ts`

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.test.ts` — passed; 1 file, 3 tests passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.process.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` — passed; 1 file, 2 tests passed (real local child-process proof)
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.ts extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.test.ts extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.process.test.ts` — passed
- `git diff --check` — passed
- mutation check: forcing the stream error to reject immediately (before child close) made both real-process tests fail on the close-before-rejection assertions; reverting the mutation made the same focused tests pass

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Microsoft Foundry `az login --use-device-code` stdout/stderr stream errors are contained without an unhandled stream error, duplicate teardown, or settlement before the child closes.
Real environment tested: local Linux Node source checkout; the proof uses a PATH-injected local `az` substitute executable — a real spawned process with real stdio pipes, not the Azure CLI and not an in-process mocked child.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.process.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose`.
Evidence after fix: `[proof] local az substitute pid=3820935 forced stdout stream error contained; close observed before rejection` and `[proof] local az substitute pid=3820960 ignored SIGTERM; SIGKILL escalation closed child before rejection`; `Test Files 1 passed (1); Tests 2 passed (2)`.
Observed result after fix: the first forced stdout stream error is reported as `az login stdout stream failed`, duplicate stderr stream errors are ignored, the promise does not reject before child `close`, and a SIGTERM-ignoring substitute is escalated to SIGKILL before rejection.
What was not tested: a live Azure CLI/device-code authentication and a kernel-originated stdout read error — Node offers no reliable local way to force a kernel read error on `child.stdout`, so the test drives the real exported function with a real child process and forces the Node stream error on that real pipe.
